# Roleplay Rule 6 - Antagonists are run by the GMs On Sector Vestige, antagonists are part of a story, and the Game Masters (GMs) are the ones telling it. You are only an antagonist if the game or a GM tells you that you are one. Antagonists are watched by the GMs, and their direction comes before anything else on this page.
## If you are an antagonist - Follow GM direction. If a GM tells you how loud, how violent or how fast to play, that is the line. If you are unsure how far you can go, ask through ahelp before you act, not after. - Play the role you were given. Don't take or enable antagonist roles you don't want to play, and don't throw the role away by ignoring it. - Work with your team. As a team antagonist, don't sabotage, betray or ignore your own team unless a GM says otherwise. Solo antagonists may betray other antagonists when it suits their story. - Keep the damage to your story. Death and destruction should serve your objectives or your GM's direction. Wiping out departments or people who were never part of your story is not antagonism, it is ending everyone else's scene. - Give people something to react to. An antagonist is there to create conflict for others to roleplay with, not to win as quickly as possible. See [textlink="Guideline 3" link="GuidelineG3"].
## If you are not an antagonist - Don't act like one. Starting a cult or revolution, mutinying, sabotaging station systems or handing out access is antagonist behaviour and needs a GM or the game to sanction it. - Small, in-character trouble is fine: stealing a glass from the bar, a hallway argument, a petty grudge. Big trouble is the GMs' to hand out. - Don't willfully help known antagonists unless your character has a real in-character reason and a GM is aware of it.
If something you want to do would change the shift for a lot of other players, it is a GM's call. Ahelp and ask.
